newsitem.title: CHINA: PRESS DIGEST - HK newspaper headlines - July 29.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - HK newspaper headlines - July 29.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Hong Kong press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

-- MING PAO -- In the first reshuffle of senior officials in the Special Administrative Region (SAR) government, Secretary for Transport Gordon Siu became chief of the Central Policy Unit. Many officials predicted Siu will be the successor to Chief Secretary Anson Chan.

-- APPLE DAILY -- Legal experts said if the SAR government loses a legal battle over the legality of the post-handover Provisional Legislature, the legal chaos would not be as serious as described by the government.

-- WEN WEI PO -- Chinese Vice-Premier Zhu Rongji said China's economic development was becoming stable and he predicted economic growth could be maintained at a minimum rate of eight percent per year.
-- TA KUNG PAO -- Liu Zhenwu, leader of the Hong Kong garrison of the People's Liberation Army, has been promoted to lieutenant-general. He urged his troops to obey the law.

-- EXPRESS NEWS -- Six European countries have rejected visa applications from holders of a type of Hong Kong travel document called a Document of Identity. Some mainland immigrants who have been in Hong Kong for less than seven years accused the countries for not respecting their human rights.
-- APPLE DAILY -- The southern Chinese city of Shenzhen closed down five drug rehabilitation centres because some had become drug trafficking centres.
-- ECONOMIC JOURNAL -- The Hong Kong Monetary Authority warned that banks would be punished if they violated its mortgage lending guidelines.

-- SOUTH CHINA MORNING POST -- Secretary for Financial Services Rafael Hui said the long-awaited Mandatory Provident Fund draft legislation was expected to be handed to the Provisional Legislature for approval within the next two months.

-- HONGKONG STANDARD -- The Financial Services Bureau said it would ask the Stock Exchange of Hong Kong to explain a delay in the submission of a key report on lowering transaction costs if it did not hear from the exchange by Thursday.
